mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 4.5% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as investors seek yield in equities during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS remains below 4.5% over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 20-day returns as corporate earnings expectations decline.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.0% over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate weakening consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 20-day returns as corporate earnings forecasts adjust downward.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) falling below 100 (index) during late-cycle expansion signals manufacturing slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns as recession risks increase.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO falls below 100 during late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth rate (GDPC1) rising above 3.0% annually indicates expanding economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns through sustained corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth exceeds 3.0% in more than 60% of cases but SPX 60-day returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate exceeding 5.0% signals aggressive monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and causing negative S&P 500 20-day returns as bond yields rise.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate above 5.0% combined with high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) signals dual stress in labor markets and monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 5-day returns as volatility spikes.
failure_condition: The joint condition of UNRATE > 5.0% and FEDFUNDS > 4.5% fails to produce negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 and housing starts (HOUST) declining from 12-month peaks during manufacturing slowdown regimes signal deepening economic contraction, causing negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO and HOUST both decline from 12-month peaks.
